statement: Greedy (smallest-available-color) vertex coloring uses at most chi(G)+1 colors on every graph, whatever order the vertices are processed in.
definitions: Greedy colouring: process the vertices in a given order and assign each the smallest positive integer not already used on its previously coloured neighbours. chi(G) = chromatic number. Graph finite simple undirected.
ground_truth_witness: The crown graph S_4 (= K_{4,4} minus a perfect matching): U = {u0,u1,u2,u3}, V = {v0,v1,v2,v3}, edges ui-vj for all i != j (12 edges). It is bipartite, so chi = 2. Process the vertices in the interleaved order u0, v0, u1, v1, u2, v2, u3, v3: greedy assigns u0=1, v0=1, u1=2, v1=2, u2=3, v2=3, u3=4, v3=4, using 4 colors > chi+1 = 3. (The same construction with k pairs makes greedy use k colors instead of 2.)
reference_authority: online-cited counterexample (MO/MSE/CS.SE/Wikipedia) with verify script, verified per partB_feasibility records

skeptic.objection: Precise and false. Verified the greedy trace on the crown graph S_4 (bipartite, chi=2) in the interleaved order: colours 1,1,2,2,3,3,4,4, i.e. 4 > chi+1 = 3. Refuting needs a graph plus an adversarial order and a trace - a genuine construction (the generic 'greedy uses at most Delta+1' knowledge does not hand it over). Roster has greedy items for knapsack, vertex cover, interval scheduling but no greedy-colouring item; no duplicate.
skeptic.suggested_definitions: Greedy colouring: process the vertices in a given order and assign each the smallest positive integer not already used on its previously coloured neighbours. chi(G) = chromatic number. Graph finite simple undirected.
